subject: Revenue commitment review — pricing lag risks for Q4
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Revenue commitment review — pricing lag risks for Q4

Team,

Quick one: finance flagged a set of pending approvals that are currently preventing us from counting ~ $680k toward our Q4 committed revenue. I pulled the list below from HubSpot; these are mostly pricing / discount approvals stuck in deal desk or waiting on procurement signatures at the customer. If we don't clear these by EOD Fri they will fall out of the commit and materially change the forecast.

Top five at-risk deals (high-level):
- VEL-2026-042 — Velotech Systems — MQL to Contract; waiting Deal Desk approval for 18% discount vs list. (ARR: $420k)
- NOV-2026-301 — NovaPower — awaiting procurement PO & legal redline. (ARR: $120k)
- MUST-PTL — Mustang Pilot — pricing variance needs deal desk sign-off. (ARR: $85k)
- ACME-BIO-2 — Acme Bio — legal requested retention term tweak; deal desk review queued. (ARR: $35k)

Ask: can Deal Desk (Marissa) triage VEL-2026-042 and confirm whether the 18% discount can be approved under the existing playbook, or whether we need escalation to finance for one-time concession? Ben / Karthik — please confirm latest customer signatures/PO status for Velotech and attach the term sheet if available.

I will compile a short commit update for the revenue call on Friday morning.

Thanks,

Mina Haddad
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: VEL-2026-042_term_sheet_v2.pdf (term sheet stub), VEL-summary-q4-pipeline.xlsx (pipeline extract)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Revenue commitment review — pricing lag risks for Q4

Mina — thanks for the heads up. Quick updates: 

- Velotech (VEL-2026-042): They verbally agreed to proceed after our QBR last week; procurement requested a formal term sheet and then asked for an additional 3% off to hit an internal budget number. I uploaded the latest term sheet to the deal (attached). Customer sign-in is pending PO; they said they can push PO by Wednesday if we lock the pricing.
- NovaPower: PO in process; procurement legal back-and-forth on retention clause.
- Mustang Pilot: still in pilot; discount request from the buyer's org lead for a pilot uplift — flagged to product and deal desk.

For Velotech specifically, we have some precedent for 18% on enterprise pilots when we include a 12-month commit and a support add-on. If Deal Desk can approve with the standard concession authority, I'll ask the customer to send the PO today. If not, we'll need fast finance sign-off.

Attaching: VEL-2026-042_term_sheet_v2.pdf

—Ben
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

>

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T15:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Revenue commitment review — pricing lag risks for Q4

Thanks for the detail. I reviewed VEL-2026-042 and the attached term sheet. Two notes: 

1) Under our current pricing playbook the maximum standard concession for a 12-month contract without CRO approval is 15%. The 18% Ben states exceeds the playbook.
2) The deal economics include a support bundle that could be structured as an add-on to preserve list pricing for the core product while meeting the customer's target TCO.

Actions I can take immediately:
- Approve up to 15% now to keep the deal soft-committed (no finance escalation).
- If the seller wants to keep 18%, I need a formal request with margin impact and product approval; I can fast-track to Finance for one-time concession.

Ben — please confirm whether the customer will accept a 15% structure with a support add-on, or whether they insist on 18%. If they insist, attach the commercial justification and I'll route to Finance (cc'd: finance alias on escalation).

I'll queue the fast-track packet this afternoon if we get the justification.

Marissa Cole
Deal Desk Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: Alicia Ramos <alicia@velotech.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, procurement@velotech.com
Cc: J. Park, CFO <j.park@velotech.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T16:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Revenue commitment review — pricing lag risks for Q4

Hi Ben / team — apologies for the delay. We can move forward with a PO this week if Redwood can accept 16% off list and include the enterprise support bundle at the quoted rates. Internal procurement pushed back on anything higher than 16% because of our headcount freeze.

If Redwood counters with 15% + the support add-on (as Marissa suggested), I need a final doc by EOD Thursday to route to legal and secure the PO by Friday. Prefer not to escalate to their CFO but I can if product procurement requires.

Please advise next steps and share the final term sheet.

Thanks,
Alicia Ramos
Head of IT Procurement
Velotech Systems
